solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lacking cash, dealer finally becomes agent

parts.note: someone lacking cash is broke, penniless

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word dealer

explanation.surface: A dealer who has run out of money ends up working on commission for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker is an intermediary who acts on behalf of clients, which is what an agent does.

clue.text: Pester Republican with emblem of office

parts.note: a badge is a token worn to show rank or office

explanation.surface: Someone harasses a Republican politician who wears the insignia of his post.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue as R then BADGE, but 'with' just joins them; the answer puts the emblem first.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester and to badger are synonyms: both mean to nag persistently.

clue.text: Extremely tired, moor our boat badly, having portable engine

indicators.note: done badly, the letters are jumbled into a new order
the extremes of the word tired are its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: An exhausted sailor makes a poor job of tying up, but the boat has a detachable motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes TD, the outer letters of 'tired'; 'badly' mixes TD with MOOROURBOAT to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An outboard motor is a self-contained engine clamped to a boat's stern and lifted off when needed, hence portable.

clue.text: Ahead of time, almost not having started

indicators.note: a word that has not started has lost its opening letter

parts.note: almost means nearly

explanation.surface: Someone is almost there before the off, yet hasn't even begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having started' removes the first letter N from NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving early means turning up before the appointed hour, a straight synonym.

clue.text: College boy's agreement

parts.note: uni is the casual short form of university, a college
a son is a male child, a boy

explanation.surface: A university student gives his consent to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting in complete accord, so the word stands for concord or agreement.

clue.text: Win over artist capturing a N American river

indicators.note: capturing means holding something within, so the letter goes inside
over signals the word is turned round, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to win something is to gain it
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone persuades a painter, who seizes something, near an American waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the synonym of 'Win' round, and 'capturing' means the reversed word and the artist together hold the letter A between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niagara is the river joining Lakes Erie and Ontario, famous for its falls on the US–Canada border.

clue.text: Random winnings help, securing English seamstress's device

indicators.note: securing means holding fast within, so one letter is placed inside the rest
random signals the letters fall in no set order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seamstress's lucky prize money pays for a new machine from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Random' rearranges WINNINGSHELP; 'securing' puts E inside that mix to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning wheel is a hand- or foot-powered machine for twisting fibre into thread, a tool of textile work.

clue.text: French city where granny put up?

parts.note: nan is a familiar British word for grandmother

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to put something somewhere is to set it there

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about the French town where Grandma was given lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a major port city on the Loire in western France.

clue.text: Resolve to put off race across motorway

indicators.note: the two words lie across, straddling, the motorway, so it sits between them

parts.note: to put someone off doing something is to deter them
a race of people is a nation
M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A plan to discourage a running event from crossing a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: MI stands for the M1, the British motorway from London to Leeds; 'across' sets DETER and NATION either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve as a noun is firmness of purpose, a synonym of steadfastness or will.

clue.text: Like noodles, possibly, heading for trouble!

definitions.meaning: noodles may literally be found floating in a broth
the idiom describes being in a mess or a tight spot

explanation.surface: Noodles might seem destined for disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in serious difficulty, while literally pasta strands sit in a bowl of broth.

clue.text: European introducing lousy sort of resin

parts.note: poxy is British slang for rubbish or lousy

explanation.surface: A European brings in a substandard kind of resin.
explanation.walkthrough: POXY is informal British for worthless or rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Epoxy is a thermosetting polymer used as a strong adhesive and coating, a type of resin.

clue.text: Apprentice gunners at home entertained by Peg

indicators.note: something entertained by a host is taken in, so these letters go within

parts.note: a tee is the small peg a golf ball rests on
RA, the Royal Artillery, are the gunners
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A young artillery recruit is being hosted at home by a woman called Peg.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery are the British army's gunners. 'Peg' looks like a woman's name but is the golf peg; 'entertained by' puts the gunners and 'at home' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a learner being taught a trade, so a trainee is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Make-up from EU country reportedly reaching father in time

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, by ear rather than as written

parts.note: Greece is a member state of the European Union
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Cosmetics brought from a European nation reach Dad just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means the name of the country is heard, giving GREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasepaint is the thick theatrical cosmetic actors wear on stage, so it is a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Eg East Grinstead in relation to its Great Danes?

definitions.text: Eg East Grinstead in relation to its Great Danes?

parts.words: Eg East Grinstead in relation to its Great Danes
parts.note: the letters of the town's name rearrange to spell ITS GREAT DANES, so the town is a reshuffle of that phrase

explanation.surface: It sounds like a question about a Sussex town's population of large dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: East Grinstead is a town in West Sussex; its thirteen letters are exactly those of ITS GREAT DANES, the joke being that it is a word-shuffle of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase made by rearranging another's letters is the term for such a reshuffle; the clue gives an example.

clue.text: Bluff son identifying coastal features?

parts.note: a bluff is a steep headland or bank, a cliff

explanation.surface: A boy pretends to be someone else, and is found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff' looks like deceit but is the noun, a steep bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliffs are steep rock faces typical of the shoreline, so they are examples of seaside landforms.

clue.text: Press chief possibly cycled up carrying it

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the word goes inside
in a down clue, up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a cyclist who cycled rode a bike

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss perhaps pedalled uphill while hauling something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives EDOR, read upwards in this down clue; 'carrying' means that reversed word holds the clue's own 'it' in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a newspaper's journalistic staff is its editor, one example of a press chief, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Posh doctor engaged by prisoner over back pain

indicators.note: letters engaged by another word are taken into it, held inside

parts.note: lag is British slang for a convict, especially an old lag
U denotes upper-class, posh, usage
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: An upper-class medic is hired by a jailbird to treat his aching back.
explanation.walkthrough: U means upper-class in British usage; 'engaged by' puts UMB inside LAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the muscles and joints of the lower back.

clue.text: Browbeaten commander tied the knot

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer
to tie the knot is to get married, to wed

explanation.surface: An officer who married was dominated by his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone browbeaten has been intimidated into submission, which is what cowed means.

clue.text: Cut up rough at first in underground hollow

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cave is a hollow beneath the ground

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word rough

explanation.surface: Things got violent early on in a cavern below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve meat is to slice it, to cut up a joint into portions.

clue.text: Exceptionally rosy prediction — but it makes us tense

definitions.meaning: a forecast of times ahead that are flawless
a grammatical tense, as in 'we will have finished'

explanation.surface: An unusually optimistic forecast leaves us anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervousness but is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as words, a flawless time ahead; as grammar, the verb form for actions completed before a later point, like 'will have gone'.

clue.text: Tiny kid getting quiet parent initially on edge

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a rim is an edge or border

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word parent

explanation.surface: A small child gets hushed by a mum or dad who is feeling nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' looks like anxiety, but 'edge' is a piece and 'on' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is an informal, affectionate term for a very small person, especially a child.

clue.text: Popular chap who cuts down trees?

definitions.meaning: a colloquial, popular-speech form of fellow, a man
a lumberjack, one who fells timber

explanation.surface: A well-liked man who works as a lumberjack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular' here means in everyday, informal speech, not well-liked.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a casual spelling of fella for a man, and also the noun for one who fells trees.
